title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Headline metrics hide systematic miscalibration, and even simple post-hoc recalibration often reduces it, with the largest gains where error is worst.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter panels, diagonal reference line, shaded improvement region
description: Two side-by-side scatter plots of hexagonal markers, colored by uncertainty-representation category: blue is parametric, orange is discretized, green is direct quantile, purple is generative. The left panel, titled 'Full Gap: PCE_pool ≤ QCE_avg', plots pooled unconditional calibration error on the x-axis against conditional QCE_avg on the y-axis. Almost every point lies above the dashed diagonal. The right panel is titled 'Recalibration (Isotonic recalibration, chronological split)'. It plots PCE_avg before recalibration against PCE_avg after recalibration. The area below the diagonal is shaded light green and labeled 'improved ↓'. Many points fall in that region, especially those with large initial error. Each panel has a legend, and the dense cluster of points near the origin draws the eye first.
caption: Overview of the proposed calibration evaluation framework and main empirical findings. Left: Relationship between \( \mathrm{PCE}_{\mathrm{pool}} \) and \( \mathrm{QCE}_{\mathrm{avg}} \) across model-dataset pairs. All points lie above the diagonal, consistent with the calibration hierarchy \( \mathrm{PCE}_{\mathrm{pool}} \le \mathrm{QCE}_{\mathrm{avg}} \), showing that pooled probabilistic calibration can substantially understate miscalibration once horizon-specific and quantile-conditioned effects are taken into account. Right: Effect of post-hoc isotonic recalibration on \( \mathrm{PCE}_{\mathrm{avg}} \), fitted on the earliest 20% of the forecast windows and evaluated on the later ones. Points below the diagonal improve (62% of the model--dataset pairs), and the largest gains occur where the original miscalibration is most severe, indicating that even simple recalibration techniques often improve horizon-wise probabilistic calibration in practice.
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that current models exhibit distinct and systematic patterns of miscalibration that standard metrics often obscure. We further analyze common post-hoc recalibration methods and characterize which forms of calibration they can improve and which tend to persist. Our results provide practical guidance for evaluating and improving uncertainty calibration in TSFMs and highlight important limitations of current practice.
